task.description:
Hard-gate CODE-DESIGNER's §10 addition to lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md (commit 3cfdaf7b on this branch) -- the ISS-0480 structural fix (a new Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo, TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 redirected to it via Ecto.Repo.put_dynamic_repo/1 instead of calling Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) directly). Read §10 in full (sections 10.0-10.7, roughly lines 948-1679) plus §§0-9 for context on the design lineage and the reverted restore_sandbox mechanism this design must not resemble. Do not accept CODE-DESIGNER's own result.summary as sufficient -- independently re-derive each of the following against the actual design text and, where a claim is checkable against real library source or arithmetic, against that source/arithmetic directly, per this project's 're-derive under the conditions the property is actually about' standard (core-directives.md).

SPECIFIC CLAIMS TO INDEPENDENTLY VERIFY, NOT TRUST:
1. The DBConnection.Ownership.Manager scoping claim -- that a Sandbox.mode/2 call issued against a SEPARATE Ecto.Repo (Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo, its own pool/supervisor) cannot check in connections belonging to a DIFFERENT repo's (Letflow.Repo's) pool. Check this against actual Ecto/DBConnection source (deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/sql/sandbox.ex and deps/db_connection, same standard ISSUE-FIXER's own diagnosis used) -- do not accept the design's own citation without opening the source yourself.
2. The pool-budget arithmetic in design section 10.2.2 -- the claimed connection counts (34 total at plain `mix test`, aggregate worst case 80 vs usable ceiling 97 at test_parallel.sh N=16) and the reconciliation against decision 0009-test-parallel-pool-sizing.md's existing formula. Recompute independently from the design's own stated inputs; flag any arithmetic error found, however small.
3. That NO second Sandbox.mode/2 call is added anywhere against Letflow.Repo specifically -- grep/read the design's own normative section (10.3) for every Sandbox.mode/2 or put_dynamic_repo/1 call site it specifies, and confirm none of them targets Letflow.Repo in a way that reintroduces ISS-0113's reverted mechanism-4 (a second mid-test mode flip on the SAME repo the outer test already checked a connection out of).
4. That the design's own claim -- a narrow per-call-site conversion tranche cannot ever fully protect a file with zero TenantFixture involvement -- is actually argued, not merely asserted (design section 10.0). This determines whether ISS-0480 can be marked `resolved` (this design ships and works) vs. only ever `instrumented` (if the reasoning doesn't actually hold up) -- get this right, since ORCH's later status decision depends on your verdict here.
5. Public API/error-taxonomy preservation (design section 10.4) -- confirm provisioned_tenant!/1's @spec, opts() type and return shape are genuinely unchanged in the design's own normative section, and that none of the 46 existing call sites need any edit.
6. The regression-test mechanism in section 10.6 -- confirm it is genuinely deterministic (constructs the adversarial concurrent-caller scenario directly via Task.async, not suite-timing-dependent) and that it would plausibly fail pre-fix and pass post-fix as claimed, reasoning through the actual mechanism rather than taking the design's own claim at face value.

Apply the same FAIL discipline as any other gate: if any claim above does not hold up under your own re-derivation, this is a BLOCKER, named specifically (which claim, what you found instead), not a general impression. A PASS must state what you independently re-derived and how (per this project's own worked PASS example in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md), not merely 'looks correct.'
acceptance_criteria: DBConnection.Ownership.Manager per-repo scoping independently confirmed against actual Ecto/DBConnection source, not the design's own citation alone
Pool-budget arithmetic (design 10.2.2) independently recomputed from stated inputs, any discrepancy named
Confirmed no second Sandbox.mode/2 call targets Letflow.Repo anywhere in the design's normative section 10.3
The 'narrow conversion cannot ever fully protect an uninvolved file' claim independently assessed as sound or not, with reasoning stated either way
provisioned_tenant!/1's public API/error taxonomy confirmed unchanged in the design's own normative text
Regression-test mechanism (10.6) assessed for genuine determinism, not suite-timing luck
Any BLOCKER named specifically enough for CODE-DESIGNER to act on without further clarification

result.summary:
PASS on all 6 checkable claims of design §10, each independently re-derived against real source/arithmetic, not accepted from CODE-DESIGNER's own citation.

1. DBConnection.Ownership.Manager scoping -- CONFIRMED against actual source, read directly, not the design's citation alone. `Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode/2` (deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/sql/sandbox.ex:509-516) resolves `%{pid: pool}` via `lookup_meta!(repo)` -- keyed on the SPECIFIC repo module argument -- then calls `DBConnection.Ownership.ownership_mode(pool, mode, opts)` (deps/db_connection/lib/db_connection/ownership.ex:125-127, `defdelegate ownership_mode(manager, mode, opts), to: Manager, as: :mode`), which sends the mode-change to THAT `manager` GenServer pid specifically. Read `Manager.handle_call({:mode, mode}, {caller, _}, state)` directly (deps/db_connection/lib/db_connection/ownership/manager.ex:165-172): `proxy_checkin_all_except(state, [], caller)` iterates `state.checkouts` (line 299-308) -- that Manager process's OWN state, not a global/shared table. Since `Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo` is a distinct `Ecto.Repo` module (§10.3.1) with its own `pool_size`/adapter config (§10.3.4), `lookup_meta!(Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo)` resolves a DIFFERENT `pid: pool` than `lookup_meta!(Letflow.Repo)`, hence a wholly separate Manager GenServer with its own, disjoint `checkouts` map. A `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo, :auto)` call structurally cannot check in any connection recorded in `Letflow.Repo`'s own Manager's `checkouts` map -- confirmed by the source, not merely the design's quoted excerpt (which matched verbatim what I read independently). Also independently confirmed `Ecto.Repo.put_dynamic_repo/1` (deps/ecto/lib/ecto/repo.ex:314-316) is `Process.put({__MODULE__, :dynamic_repo}, dynamic)` -- genuinely process-scoped, matching §10.3.2's claim.

2. Pool-budget arithmetic (§10.2.2) -- recomputed independently from the design's own stated inputs (schedulers=16, TEST_MAX_CONNECTIONS=100, TEST_SUPERUSER_RESERVED=3, TEST_CONNECTION_HEADROOM=10, TEST_NONPOOL_CONNECTION_RESERVE=2, PROVISIONING_POOL_SIZE=2, N=16), via a fresh bash arithmetic script (not re-typing the design's numbers back): plain-mix-test total = 32+2 = 34 (matches); usable_ceiling = 100-3 = 97 (matches); pre-extension budget = 97-10-2 = 85 (matches decision 0009's own addendum figure, itself independently checked against docs/migration/decisions/0009-test-parallel-pool-sizing.md's addendum text); pre-extension computed = 85/16 = 5 (matches, and matches decision 0009's own verification); extended budget' = 85-(16*2) = 53 (matches); computed' = 53/16 = 3 integer division (matches); aggregate worst case = 16*(3+2) = 80 (matches); slack vs usable_ceiling 97 = 17 (matches). Zero discrepancies found in any of the 8 recomputed figures. Also cross-checked config/test.exs:75-79's actual `pool_size` formula (`schedulers_online()*2` / `TEST_POOL_SIZE` override) and scripts/test_parallel.sh:150-164's actual clamp formula (`usable_ceiling`/`budget`/`computed_pool`/floor) by direct read -- both match exactly what the design cites as the pre-existing formula being extended.

3. No second Sandbox.mode/2 against Letflow.Repo -- confirmed by reading every Sandbox.mode/2 and put_dynamic_repo/1 call site named in §10.3 (the only normative section): §10.3.2 item 1 REMOVES the existing `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)` line outright; item 2 adds exactly one new call, `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo, :auto)`, targeting the new repo only; items 3-6 use `put_dynamic_repo/1` (a process-dictionary binding, not a Sandbox-mode call) alternating between `ProvisioningRepo` and restoring `Letflow.Repo` as the DEFAULT dynamic repo -- this is not a `Sandbox.mode/2` call of any kind, and does not re-flip `Letflow.Repo`'s own sandbox mode. No call site in §10.3 issues `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, ...)` anywhere after the initial removal. ISS-0113's reverted mechanism-4 (a second mid-test mode flip on the SAME repo the outer test already checked a connection out of) requires a second `Sandbox.mode/2` call targeting `Letflow.Repo` specifically -- confirmed absent.

4. The 'narrow conversion can never fully protect an uninvolved file' claim -- independently assessed as SOUND, and it is genuinely argued (not merely asserted) in §10.0: the argument traces that today's hazard is not proportional to conversion count (the 2 ALREADY-shipped files are what ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis caught firing against RowApprovalTest, a file with zero TenantFixture involvement), that §9.4's own safety proof only established MUTUAL safety among TenantFixture callers (never tested against an unrelated async:true file, because ISS-0423's scope had none), and that the ONLY way a narrow approach could close this is reverting to zero async:true TenantFixture callers entirely -- which is stated as unacceptable (reverts ISS-0423's shipped, measured throughput win). I re-traced this chain against §9.1/§9.3/§9.4's own mechanism (independently read, not merely re-quoted) and it holds: since `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)`'s check-in is global/pool-wide with an empty exclusion list (confirmed directly in manager.ex, see claim 1), and reachable from ANY TenantFixture-calling file's own async execution, a victim file's exposure is binary (exists once any TenantFixture caller is async:true) not gradual. The reasoning is sound; ISS-0480 can be marked resolved only if this structural fix ships, matching the design's own conclusion.

5. Public API/error-taxonomy preservation -- confirmed directly against current `test/support/tenant_fixture.ex`: `@spec provisioned_tenant!(opts()) :: tenant_fixture()` (line 220) and `@type opts` (lines 74-81, no `restore_sandbox` key present, matching §9.6's already-shipped removal) match byte-for-byte what §10.4 claims is preserved; §10.3.2 adds nothing to `opts()`. Recounted call sites independently: `grep -rl "provisioned_tenant!(" test --include=*.exs` excluding the definition file = 46 files, exactly matching the design's own count -- confirming 'zero call-site edits needed' is checkable and the count is accurate.

6. Regression-test mechanism (§10.6) -- assessed as genuinely deterministic, not suite-timing luck. Read test/support/data_case.ex:15-23 directly: confirms `async: true` tests get an unconditional, un-shared `Sandbox.checkout(Letflow.Repo)` with no `{:shared, self()}` call -- exactly the precondition §10.6's design assumes for the outer test process. The mechanism (spawn a Task.async that directly calls provisioned_tenant!/1, manufacturing the adversarial concurrent-caller scenario rather than waiting for ExUnit scheduling luck) is a real construction, not a description of hoped-for timing -- it directly forces the exact call (`Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)` pre-fix / `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo, :auto)` post-fix) whose effect is under test. Pre-fix failure mode reasoning checks out mechanically against manager.ex's actual check-in behavior (claim 1): the outer test's checkout would be discarded via the same `proxy_checkin_all_except` path. The design appropriately hedges rather than overclaiming ('This must actually be run against current main to confirm it fails before being trusted as a regression test' -- §10.6) rather than asserting the pre-fix failure as already proven without running it, which is the correct posture for a design artefact per this project's design/implementation split.

No BLOCKER found. Design §10 is unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without further judgement calls (module/config/seam signatures fully specified in §10.3.1-10.3.4, open questions in §10.7 explicitly flagged rather than silently resolved, none of them ambiguous about WHAT ships, only about implementer-discretion naming/organization choices).
result.next_action: Route to ELIXIR-DEV to implement design §10: new test-only Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo module, TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1's internal put_dynamic_repo/1 seam (public API unchanged, confirmed), config/test.exs sibling config block, scripts/test_parallel.sh TEST_POOL_SIZE formula extension by PROVISIONING_POOL_SIZE=2. ORCH's later status decision may treat ISS-0480 as resolvable (not merely instrumented) once this design ships and TEST-RUNNER's real double full-suite run (§10.7 OQ-9) confirms it under actual execution -- this gate confirms only that the design itself is sound, not that ELIXIR-DEV's implementation of it is.
